● Buyer's guide · 6 min read

✏️ COI tracking spreadsheet, outsourced service or software: which should a GC use?

A COI tracking spreadsheet works while you have a few contractors, one set of requirements and someone who reads every endorsement. Outsource COI tracking when you need hands, not judgment. Use COI tracking software when requirements change by project, contractors work several jobs, and you want the broker fixing gaps fast.

✅ A COI tracking spreadsheet tracks dates well. It can't read an endorsement or hold different requirements for each project, so a person has to do both by hand for every contractor COI.

✅ When you outsource COI tracking, you buy capacity: collection, reminders and follow-up. Ask exactly what the service's reviewers read and who signs off, because the gap is still yours if it's missed.

● Buyer's guide · 7 min read

✏️ COI deficiency notice tools for insurance brokers (2026): what helps you answer faster

Insurance brokers answer a COI deficiency notice fastest with four kinds of tools: the agency management system that issues the corrected certificate, a certificate network that keeps it current, an outsourced certificate team for volume, and the general contractor's own portal. Most notices ask for an endorsement or a limit, so seeing the exact requirement matters most.

✅ Most COI deficiency notices ask for an endorsement or a higher limit. A corrected certificate can't add coverage, so the fix starts with the policy, and the certificate follows.

✅ Your agency management system issues the corrected certificate. Certificate networks and client self-service cut the volume, and outsourced certificate teams take the overflow.

Read the post →

● Buyer's guide · 8 min read

✏️ Best COI compliance platform for insurance brokers and general contractors to work together (2026)

The best COI compliance platform for insurance brokers and general contractors is the one where the broker sees the project requirements, the deficiency and the project in one place, and the general contractor still approves. Most broker programs let you resell or refer a tool. Fewer let you work inside the general contractor's project.

✅ COI compliance platforms work with insurance brokers in two ways: the broker resells or refers a tool to clients, or the broker works inside the general contractor's project on each gap. Most broker programs are the first kind.

✅ For collaboration on a job, the test is what the broker sees. If the broker gets the project requirements, the deficiency and the project together, the fix comes back right the first time.

Read the post →

● Tech stack · 5 min read

⚙️ Autodesk Construction Cloud COI tracking: where contractor insurance lives in Forma Build and what it checks

Autodesk Construction Cloud COI tracking, now in Forma Build, works through compliance requirements in Cost Management. A project admin requires a certificate of insurance, with an expiration date, on a contract or payment application, and the item can't be submitted until it's uploaded. TradeTapp can block a contract when insurance is missing. Nothing in Autodesk's docs reads the endorsements.

✅ Autodesk Construction Cloud COI tracking lives in Cost Management in Forma Build. Project admins set compliance requirements, such as a certificate of insurance with an expiration date, on contracts, payment applications and change orders, and the item can't be submitted until they're met.

✅ TradeTapp, Autodesk's prequalification tool, can add a condition that blocks sending a contract when a supplier's insurance documents are missing or expired. Autodesk's docs describe uploading and dating documents, not reading what the endorsements say.
